findings.issue: The `--lineage-mode` row gives the accepted values as `auto | resume | restart`, but the workflow's `lineage_mode` input accepts `completed-continue` as a fourth value, and the preflight only rejects a `lineage_mode` other than `auto` or `completed-continue` when `--extend` is bound. A reader who wants to name the extension mode explicitly is told the flag does not take it.

The runtime persists lineage events for `resume` (same sessionId, no archive), `restart` (new sessionId, generation+1, prior review/ archived) and `completed-continue` (from --extend=N: a completed run extended in place by N iterations, same sessionId and generation). `fork` is not accepted."

findings.issue: The entry states the floor unconditionally: "A STOP candidate is overridden while `iterationCount < minIterations`". `buildStopDecision` only applies the floor when `minIterations > 1`, so a config that sets `minIterations` to 1 (the workflow clamps the effective floor to the inclusive range 0..max_iterations, so 1 is a legal value) never blocks a stop candidate. The doc claims a behavior the code does not have for that value.

The page states the floor unconditionally: "a STOP candidate is blocked while the completed iteration count is below the effective floor". `buildStopDecision` guards the floor with `minIterations > 1`, so an effective floor of 1 (a legal value: the workflow clamps it to 0..max_iterations) never blocks a stop candidate. The page claims to describe the shipped floor rule in full and omits that guard.
